# The runtime map

**Generated by `tools/build_runtimes.py` from `ops/RUNTIMES.tsv`. Do not hand-edit.**

`ops/PORTS.tsv` records where a surface *listens*. Until 2026-09-10 nothing recorded
what runs behind it, what invokes it, what it loads, or whether it takes the GPU lease —
those answers lived in `api.py`'s argv builders, `gpu-governor.sh`'s `case` arms,
`restore/manifests/BUILD-RECIPES.tsv` and nowhere respectively.

The **decisions** are in `ops/RUNTIMES.tsv`. The **measurements** below are read off the
disk by the generator on every run, because a size or a build date in a hand-maintained
file goes stale silently. There is no timestamp in this file on purpose: its date is the
date of the commit that carries it — `git log -1 docs/ops/RUNTIMES.md`.

**Not to be confused with `docs/ops/RUNTIME-PROFILES.md`**, whose name is one word away
and whose first line says *"Status: stub. A contract for something not yet built."* That
file is a maturity ladder for runtimes that mostly do not exist here, written against the
old `engines/symoneural-*` layout. This file is a reading of what is on this disk today.
Neither supersedes the other; they answer different questions, and reading one as the
other is the mistake their names invite.

The key is **(runtime, surface)**, not runtime. `symoneural-diffuse` serves `image` and
`sigil` from the same binary and the same weights under two governor surfaces with two
eviction arms; one row would hide the sigil surface from the eviction logic.

## Which CUDA each engine actually links, and why it depends on who starts it

`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` outranks `DT_RUNPATH` in the loader's search order. An interactive
shell on this box exports `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64`; **the systemd units export
no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` at all** (measured from `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the running API).
So the same binary can link a different CUDA depending on whether a person or the unit
started it — which means *where you test an engine changes what you are testing*.

| binary | RUNPATH | in a shell | under systemd | same? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `symoneural-llm/build/bin/symoneural-llm` | `$ORIGIN:` | 13.4 (via the `/usr/local/cuda` alternative) | 13.4 (via the `/usr/local/cuda` alternative) | yes |
| `symoneural-diffuse/build/bin/symoneural-diffuse` | `/usr/local/cuda-13.3/targets/x86_64-linux/lib:` | 13.4 (via the `/usr/local/cuda` alternative) | 13.3 | no — **they differ** |
| `symoneural-miner/build/kawpowminer/symoneural-miner` | `/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs:` | 13.4 (via the `/usr/local/cuda` alternative) | 13.4 (via the `/usr/local/cuda` alternative) | yes |

Binaries with no row above link no CUDA at all: `symoneural-listen` is CPU-only by
design, and `symoneural-web` and `symoneural-gateway` are a Go and a Rust service.

Four things follow from that table, and none of them was written down anywhere:

1. **`symoneural-diffuse` is the only one that diverges, and testing it in a shell
   tests the wrong thing.** Its RUNPATH pins CUDA 13.3 — the version it was compiled
   against — and production, started by systemd with no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, gets 13.3. A
   person running it from a terminal gets 13.4, because `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` outranks the
   RUNPATH. `restore/manifests/BUILD-RECIPES.tsv` already warns that a restored machine
   needs CUDA at that exact absolute path; this is the same fact from the other end.
2. **`symoneural-llm` was built with nvcc 13.3 and links 13.4 in both environments.**
   Nothing pins it: its `$ORIGIN` RUNPATH covers only the libraries beside it, and
   `libcudart`/`libcublas`/`libcublasLt` come from `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/000_cuda.conf`,
   which points at `/usr/local/cuda` → `/etc/alternatives/cuda` → 13.4. So
   `update-alternatives --set cuda` silently changes which CUDA the chat engine links,
   with no rebuild and no warning. That is worth knowing before anyone tidies up the
   two CUDA installs.
3. **The toolkit moved after the engines were built, and nothing recorded it.**
   `nvcc` is now `13.4 (V13.4.59)` and the driver is `615.71.09`; the
   `/etc/alternatives/cuda` symlink that decides all of the above was last written
   `2026-09-09` and points at `/usr/local/cuda-13.4`. The four
   engine binaries were built before that (their dates are in the artefacts table), so
   `symoneural-llm` and `symoneural-miner` are running on a CUDA minor newer than the
   one they were compiled with — silently, because nothing pins them.
   `symoneural-diffuse` is the one that is not, and only because its absolute RUNPATH
   holds it to 13.3. `restore/manifests/` still records the older pair; regenerating
   it is an eleven-minute whole-disk job and is nobody's side effect.
4. **The build recipe's note about `$ORIGIN` overstates it.** It says of the llm engine
   that *"RUNPATH is $ORIGIN so every library it loads is one this build produced"*.
   True of its own 23 libraries; not true of its three CUDA libraries, which come from
   the system tree. Recorded here rather than edited there — that file is generated
   from `restore/lib/registry.py` and is not this section's to change.

## The GPU lease

6 of 16 rows acquire the card: **chat, comfy, image, miner, sigil, train**.

Every one of them must be known to `scripts/gpu-governor.sh` — probeable for liveness
(a `surface_pattern()` arm, or `surface_live()`'s explicit `miner` case) *and*
stoppable (an `evict()` arm, or `train`'s deliberate refusal to be evicted).
`backend/apps/test_runtimes_registry.py` asserts both, and that assertion exists because
the two-process lease proof established the cost of getting it wrong: `drain()` with no
pattern reads **every** compute context against `DRAIN_FLOOR_MIB=1024`, so a surface the
governor does not recognise falls to the `*)` default and its first acquire behind a
resident tenant is refused — correctly, and it presents as a lock bug.

Rows with no lease are design decisions, not omissions. `symoneural-listen` stays on the
CPU so a spoken sticker can transcribe while another surface holds the card;
`symoneural-ravencalc` takes no lease so it can answer while the card is loading.

## Runtimes nothing invokes

A blank cell here would read as an omission. These are findings:

- **`symoneural-code`** — Operator-invoked only; nothing in the serving path calls it. Also provides symoneural-discovery.
- **`symoneural-audit`** — The runtime behind the path-fragility ratchet. Operator-invoked; nothing starts it.
- **`symoneural-miner-core`** — NOT A RUNNABLE MINER, and the row exists to say so rather than to leave a blank cell. `bin/` holds one file and it is an end-to-end SMOKE -- loopback only, no real mining, a shape-valid wallet that is deliberately not a real address. The clean-room claim covers the Keccak only; docs/ALGORITHM-GAP.md states what is missing. It demonstrates the pipeline, not the algorithm.

## What this map does not say, and why

A blank cell that is not explained is indistinguishable from one nobody looked at.

- **`MODELS` is `—` for `symoneural-miner`, `symoneural-ui` and `training`, and each
  for a different reason.** The miner has no model file at all — kawpow generates its
  DAG. ComfyUI loads whatever a submitted graph names, at request time, so there is no
  fixed list to record. A training job's base model is chosen per job from the
  Reinforce catalogue. Only the four rows with a fixed argv can honestly name weights.
- **The live command lines were captured for two of the six leaseholders.** `chat` and
  `image` were read from `/proc` while they were actually running, and they matched the
  argv their invokers build. `miner`, `comfy` and `train` were not running and starting
  them is a deliberate act, not a measurement — that is section 2's job. Their MODELS
  and argv here are read from the call site, not from a running process.
- **No build commands.** `restore/manifests/BUILD-RECIPES.tsv` is the build authority
  and this registry names a `COMPONENT_ID` in it. Copying the command here would create
  the second copy the whole arrangement exists to prevent;
  `test_runtimes_registry.py` fails if one appears.
- **`training` has no `BUILD_RECIPE`.** It is a virtualenv, not a build product, and
  `restore/manifests/BUILD-RECIPES.tsv` has no row for it. Whether that venv is
  rebuildable is a restore-path question and belongs to the dependency inventory.
- **Nothing here says a runtime *works*.** Every cell is a fact about what is on disk
  and what calls it. `exists` and `grep` cannot ask whether a thing runs — that is
  exactly the gap the per-runtime tests are for.

## Notes, per row

- **`symoneural-llm` / chat** — LEASE_SITE names the POST /api/chat holder; `gpu.hold("chat")` appears 4 times in api.py (the WebSocket, this one, remix, and the comment in start_llama) and they are the same lease, not four. The ARTEFACT is a 17 KB SHIM, not the engine: it links libsymoneural_llm_server_impl.so with a $ORIGIN RUNPATH and the real code is 23 shared libraries beside it. Sizing this runtime by its binary understates it by three orders of magnitude. Started once and kept, then evicted by whichever surface next wants the card. LLAMA_PORT is a module constant in api.py and does NOT read the environment -- two api.py processes both serving chat would collide on 8081 regardless of the lease.
- **`symoneural-diffuse` / image** — Its RUNPATH is the ABSOLUTE /usr/local/cuda-13.3/... rather than $ORIGIN, so which CUDA it links depends on the environment it is started in -- see docs/ops/RUNTIMES.md. Runs directly inside gpu.hold, NOT wrapped in `gpu-governor.sh with`: wrapping it self-deadlocked on a lock the caller already held.
- **`symoneural-diffuse` / sigils** — Same binary and same weights as the `image` row, DIFFERENT governor surface -- deliberately, so the rack can say which of the two holds the card. It has its own eviction arm; folding it into `image` would make the surface invisible in the readout the site exists to be honest about.
- **`symoneural-listen` / sigils** — REACHABLE TODAY, ungated: POST /api/sigils/from-audio, and /api/sigils/state reports "audio": true on this box. Takes NO lease and that is the design, not an omission -- CPU transcription can run while another surface holds the card, so a spoken sticker pays only the GPU wait a typed one already pays.
- **`symoneural-listen` / voice** — The second path to the same engine. CONFIG-GATED: /api/voice/* is registered but returns a 503 naming SYMONEURAL_VOICE_ENABLED=1 and SYMONEURAL_VOICE_TOKEN, neither of which is set on this box. The code and the weights are both here; a switch is off.
- **`symoneural-miner` / gpuminer** — NOT under build/bin/ like the other three engines -- kawpowminer's CMake puts it under build/kawpowminer/, and a path built from the naming convention finds nothing. Uses the `with` form, which releases from a trap on crash; a bare acquire/release pair does not. CLEAN_BUILD_SUPPORTED=NO in BUILD-RECIPES: rebuilding needs a prebuilt static prefix and a ~40 minute two-stage job.
- **`symoneural-ui` / studio** — ComfyUI. Nothing starts it at boot and no unit exists, so `studio` reporting offline is correct rather than a fault. Its eviction arm calls symoneural-ui.sh stop and waits for the DRAIN, never a bare pkill: the process exiting is not the memory coming back.
- **`training` / train** — A separate interpreter, never the serving one: the API runs on the system python3 and this venv carries a cu128 torch stack for Blackwell sm_120. The subprocess boundary is what keeps those apart. UNIQUE among leaseholders: `train` has no eviction arm because evict() REFUSES to evict a live training run (gpu-governor.sh, before the case). That refusal is the arm.
- **`symoneural-api`** — The monolith. Every surface not marked DELEGATED in ops/PORTS.tsv answers here, and it owns the governor lease on behalf of chat, image and sigil. Runs under /usr/bin/python3 with NO LD_LIBRARY_PATH -- which is what decides symoneural-diffuse's CUDA minor.
- **`symoneural-web`** — First-party Go that imports Caddy as a library. Also binds 80 and 127.0.0.1:2019 -- see ops/PORTS.tsv; this row carries 443 because that is the one a visitor uses. TRAP: a root drop-in overrides ExecStart to serve ops/Caddyfile but leaves ExecReload pointing at /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, so `systemctl reload` silently serves the other copy. RUNBOOK.md section 6.
- **`symoneural-gateway`** — Rust, from 8 .rs files with 362 crates pinned in Cargo.lock -- NOT the thirteen TRON settlement Python modules in the same directory, which are mounted inside the API and are not what the unit runs. Its being stopped was the five-day 502.
- **`symoneural-ravencalc` / ravencalc** — THE SPLIT PILOT. Deliberately takes no lease -- that is the property that lets it answer while the card is loading. DELEGATED stays `no` in ops/PORTS.tsv until the unit is installed; flipping it first would 404 the surface on the live monolith.
- **`symoneural-cli`** — Not only an operator tool: it is the GRACEFUL half of the governor's `chat` eviction arm, with `pkill -f bin/symoneural-llm` as the ungraceful fallback. Both halves are asserted by apps/test_governor_paths.py, because a `||` fallback hides a broken primary. Installed to ~/.local/bin as a symlink, never a copy -- a copied launcher once diverged and nothing noticed for days.
- **`symoneural-code`** — Operator-invoked only; nothing in the serving path calls it. Also provides symoneural-discovery.
- **`symoneural-audit`** — The runtime behind the path-fragility ratchet. Operator-invoked; nothing starts it.
- **`symoneural-miner-core`** — NOT A RUNNABLE MINER, and the row exists to say so rather than to leave a blank cell. `bin/` holds one file and it is an end-to-end SMOKE -- loopback only, no real mining, a shape-valid wallet that is deliberately not a real address. The clean-room claim covers the Keccak only; docs/ALGORITHM-GAP.md states what is missing. It demonstrates the pipeline, not the algorithm.
